evidence.title: 日下舊聞考 大宫门
evidence.excerpt_zh: 大宫門五楹門前左右朝房各五楹其後東為宗人府内閣吏部禮部兵部都察院理藩院翰林院詹事府國子監鑾儀衛東四旗各衙門直房東夾道内為銀庫又東北為南書房東南為檔案房西為户部刑部工部欽天監内務府光禄寺通政司大理寺鴻臚寺太常寺太僕寺御書處上駟院武備院西四旗各衙門直房西夾道之西南為造辦處又南為藥房
evidence.summary: The main gate has five bays with five-bay court offices left and right. Behind them the duty rooms of the boards and offices are set out east and west by name, with the silver vault, 南書房 Southern Study and archive room to the east and the 造辦處 Imperial Workshops and pharmacy to the south-west.

evidence.title: M'Ghee: the two courts
evidence.excerpt_other: Inside the first entrance-gate there is a large, flagged courtyard, some hundred yards wide by eighty deep ; at each side, both within and without, are guard-rooms.
evidence.summary: Causeway through a sheet of water to the outer gate. A second gate of the same form, then a second court about the same size with the hall on its far side.

evidence.title: Wolseley: court and gate of 大宫门
evidence.excerpt_other: The gateway was at one end of a courtyard, enclosed upon three sides with ranges of guard-houses, handsomely ornamented outside with curious carving, and roofed with variegated tiling.
evidence.summary: Eaves with small birds and beasts, red, white, green, blue and gilt. Beam ends carved and painted. Red doors picked out in gold. Gate sills 2 or 3 ft above the pavement with granite ramps, so no wheeled traffic. Guard-room right and left within.

evidence.title: Varin: lions, dragons and the first throne hall
evidence.excerpt_other: Le mur de gauche de la salle était recouvert, dans son entier, par un seul tableau peint sur soie et représentant des vues des palais impériaux.
evidence.summary: Lions in bronze on white marble pedestals 3 m high, too heavy to carry off. Two gilt bronze dragons on the marble bridge were carried away later (his n.1). Hall reached by a wide white marble stair; black wood throne carved through, cloisonné incense burners and large enamel vases. Picture on silk.

evidence.title: Wolseley: lions at the gate
evidence.excerpt_other: the paved road leading up to the gate, upon either side of which was the colossal representation of a lion mounted upon a granite pedestal.
evidence.summary: A pair of colossal lions, bronze-coloured. Later hearsay at Shanghai that they were gold, not checked; Varin p.233 calls them bronze on white marble.

evidence.title: 6 October 1860: arrival at the Great Palace Gate
evidence.excerpt_other: A company of French marines scaled the outer wall and occupied the outer gate and courtyard on the night of October 6th, killing one or two of the defenders and suffering a few wounds themselves.
evidence.summary: French troops arrived at seven in the evening with a British cavalry brigade under Pattle. A few eunuchs defended the gate. From Cordier, quoting Montauban.

evidence.title: The Great Palace Gate and the offices before it
evidence.excerpt_other: The Great Palace Gate was a roofed building in which hung a tablet inscribed with the name of the garden, Yuan Ming Yuan, written by the Emperor K'ang Hsi.
evidence.summary: 大宫门 Da Gongmen: waiting rooms beside the road, behind them offices of the boards and the Eight Banners, the Grand Council, the 南书房 imperial school, treasury, dispensary and kitchens. Note 15 on p.70 lists the offices east and west of the gate by name.

evidence.title: 圆明园正大光明初探
evidence.summary: The whole front court district, built 1725, 370 x 310 m. 大宫门 and 出入贤良门 are five-bay gate halls with 卷棚歇山 roofs on the garden's south wall line. 正大光明殿: seven bays by three, all-round gallery, single eave, grey tile, high base, 36.45 x 16 m, with a terrace and four incense burners. Stresses its garden-like, less formal planning.

evidence.title: 大宫门考古成果 announced 2019-01-28, 中新网 via 中国日报网
evidence.summary: The park announced that the dig at 大宫门 Da Gongmen had found the gate hall, the east and west wing gates, the 金水桥 bridge and the river channel, and that the area would be conserved and opened in three display parts.

evidence.title: 正大光明区域考古勘探报告
evidence.locator: mhymy 档案史料 12324, free part
evidence.summary: Report's opening describes three successive courts from 大宫门 to 正大光明殿, 370 m north-south and 310 m east-west between the 如意门 gates, 114,700 m2 of site and 7,000 m2 of buildings, begun 1725. Gate hall of five bays on a base 21.57 x 11.33 m, 0.77 m high; screen wall 41.6 m long, 204.8 m south of the gate terrace.

searched: No picture of it found in the Forty Scenes album, its 1745 woodcuts, the Bertin gouaches and the 1887 lithograph; the 20 Xiyang Lou plates; ruin photographs on Commons, at Östasiatiska museet, the Slovene Ethnographic Museum, Historical Photographs of China, the Rijksmuseum, Wellcome and in NDL's albums of about 1900; today's photographs on Commons.
